content.title: Bachelorette Taylor Frankie Paul’s ex Dakota calls 911 after ‘violent’ fight as Mormon Wives filming screeches to a halt
content.text: BACHELORETTE Taylor Frankie Paul’s baby daddy Dakota Mortensen recently dialed 911 after an alleged violent incident at her home, The U.S. Sun has learned. Dakota reportedly called police during an altercation at The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives star Taylor‘s Utah house a few weeks ago – just as she was preparing for her on-screen debut as ABC’s The Bachelorette. Taylor Frankie Paul got into a serious altercation with her baby daddy Dakota MortensenCredit: Hulu Dakota called 911 after the fight at Taylor’s home, cops told The U.S. SunCredit: Getty Taylor and Dakota split soon after the birth of their son Ever in 2024Credit: TikTok/dakotamortensen Taylor’s debut as The Bachelorette will premiere on March 22Credit: Disney Taylor was filming Season 5 of Mormon Wives before production suddenly stoppedCredit: Disney An officer told The U.S. Sun that when cops responded to the mother-of-three’s home on February 23, violence allegations were made. “There are allegations of violence from him, but it would be fair to say the claims were made from both parties,” the officer explained. “She is alleging other things as well. It’s a complicated one. Very he said, she said.” Another law enforcement source confirmed there was a “domestic incident,” but no arrests were made. Read More Taylor Frankie Paul The first officer, however, added that there still could be an arrest, as the cops moved the case over to the prosecutor’s office for review. The case is still an ongoing and active investigation, he confirmed. Taylor’s debut as The Bachelorette begins airing on Sunday, March 22. A source close to production told The U.S. Sun that filming for The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives has been paused for the past two weeks, with the rest of the cast allegedly refusing to film. Most read in TV “Taylor is definitely in some hot water,” the insider said. They claimed the women feel production has been “protecting” Taylor in her relationship with Dakota beyond her 2023 arrest for aggravated assault. When Dakota called 911 last month, the source claimed that their toddler son, Ever, was present – and that is a big reason the rest of the cast is angry and refusing to film. The insider claimed that since all the main cast members are mothers, they are very upset and don’t want to film until the issue is properly addressed. “Everyone is refusing to film unless they can actually talk about Taylor and Dakota’s incident, and production is not going to allow that,” the source added. Taylor attended the Oscars on Sunday eveningCredit: Getty Taylor’s turn dating multiple men on camera for The Bachelorette begins this weekCredit: Getty Dakota and Taylor have been locked into a vicious up-and-down relationship for yearsCredit: Instagram/taylorfrankiepaul The insider explained that Taylor, who attended the Oscars on Sunday, is Hulu‘s “prized child.” “That’s why she gets all these opportunities. No one can really go against her, because she’s so protected by production and Hulu and Disney,” the insider added. “So now they’re all like, ‘We’ve had enough of this.’ Everyone needs to know about this. We’re not cool with this, and we’re not going to film until it gets aired out. So that’s essentially where things are.” The insider said that despite the serious allegations, they don’t believe Taylor has started drinking again. “Production has been begging everyone to film,” the insider continued. “And everyone’s like, ‘No, we’re not going to do it, until a statement gets issued about this incident.'” The insider claimed there was a similar incident that triggered Taylor’s stay at a wellness retreat at the start of Season 3. Dakota and Taylor have been at odds for years, and recently fought over custody. As exclusively revealed by The U.S. Sun, the dispute began in June when Dakota filed a petition regarding the custody of their then one-year-old son, Ever. In his filing, Dakota requested that the court formally establish custody arrangements, a visitation schedule, and child support requirements. Due to the sensitive nature of their history, the case was assigned to the most rigorous legal path in Utah, the Significant Custody Dispute Track. This classification is reserved for cases involving complex issues, including allegations of domestic violence or child abuse. The court’s decision to place the case on this track follows Taylor’s 2023 arrest after a physical altercation with Dakota. While Taylor ultimately pleaded guilty to a single charge of aggravated assault, her other domestic violence charges were dismissed as part of a plea deal. Both Dakota and Taylor were ordered to complete a mandatory parenting course and submit proof of completion to the court. Additionally, a standard Domestic Relations Injunction was issued, strictly prohibiting both parties from harassing, intimidating, or disturbing the peace of one another through any means, including digital communication. Taylor also shares two older children, Indy and Ocean, with her ex-husband, Tate Paul.
